body: Meta fell ~-77% from Sept 2021 (~$384) to an intraday low $88.09 on Nov 4 2022 (close $90.70) on Apple ATT ad-targeting losses, TikTok, the first revenue declines, ~$10bn+/yr Reality Labs losses and 2023 capex guidance near $40bn. Trough P/E ~9x, lower ex-cash. Oct 24 2022: Altimeter's Brad Gerstner published an open letter urging ~20% headcount cuts, capex cuts and capping metaverse spend at ~$5bn/yr. Nov 2022: 13% layoffs; Feb 1 2023: Zuckerberg declared 2023 the 'Year of Efficiency' with a bigger buyback (stock +23% that day [unverified]); 2023 the stock +178%, its best year. Then AI-driven ad targeting (Advantage+), Reels monetisation and margins back to ~40%+; peak ~$790s (Aug 2025) [unverified] ≈ 9x from the low. Split [approx]: EPS 2022 ~$8.6 -> 2024 ~$23.9 (~2.8x); P/E ~9x -> ~25-28x (~3x). EARLY SIGNAL visible at the trough: daily users still growing (~2bn+ DAP), engagement intact, a founder-controlled company with a cost problem that the founder could switch off, priced like a dying business; Gerstner's letter made the cost lever explicit. Who caught it: Brad Gerstner/Altimeter (documented letter, holder); 13F-tracked hedge funds bought in Q4 2022 [unverified names]. Ended: late-2025 AI capex guidance (>$100bn) pulled the stock back [unverified]. LESSON: a dominant platform at a single-digit ex-cash P/E whose problem is discretionary spending (not demand) is a high-probability turnaround once management signals cost discipline.

data.early_signals: users/engagement intact; spend-driven (not demand) problem; 9x P/E; activist letter
data.lesson: fixable cost problem in a monopoly-like platform at trough multiple

title: Meta 2022-2025: $88 trough to ~9x via 'Year of Efficiency'
